scenes.heading: Organic structure and naming
scenes.say: There are millions of carbon compounds, so chemists need a precise way to draw and name them. And because shape matters, two molecules with the same connections can act very differently in your body.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A delivery address leads any driver to exactly one house
scenes.science: An IUPAC name lets anyone rebuild exactly one structure
scenes.breaks: councils number streets however they like, but IUPAC numbering follows strict rules, and a structure has only one correct name.
scenes.say: An IUPAC name is like a delivery address. Any driver can find exactly one house, and any chemist can rebuild exactly one structure. The parent chain is the street. The locants, the numbers, are the house numbers. And the prefixes are extra details, like unit two.

scenes.heading: Naming recipe
steps: Find the longest chain containing it
Number: lowest locant to that group
scenes.say: Here's the recipe. Find the principal functional group: it becomes the suffix. Find the longest chain containing it. Number to give it the lowest locant. Add the other groups as prefixes, in alphabetical order. Then assemble: prefixes, parent, unsaturation, suffix.

scenes.heading: Worked example: two functional groups
scenes.question: Name CH₃CH(OH)CH₂C(=O)CH₃.
lines: Number from the right: C=O is C2, OH is C4
scenes.say: This molecule has an alcohol and a ketone. The ketone has higher priority, so it gets the suffix, and the alcohol becomes hydroxy. Number from the right so the carbonyl gets carbon two. The name is four hydroxy pentan two one.
scenes.caption: This molecule has an alcohol and a ketone. The ketone has higher priority, so it gets the suffix, and the alcohol becomes hydroxy. Number from the right so C=O gets C2. The name is 4-hydroxypentan-2-one.

scenes.heading: Chirality
points: Same physical properties, opposite optical rotation
scenes.say: Your hands are enantiomers: mirror images that won't stack. A carbon with four different groups is a stereocentre. Enantiomers share physical properties, but rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions, and can act differently with enzymes. With n stereocentres, you get at most two to the n stereoisomers.
scenes.caption: Your hands are enantiomers: mirror images that won't stack. A carbon with four different groups is a stereocentre. Enantiomers share physical properties, but rotate plane-polarised light in opposite directions, and can act differently with enzymes. n stereocentres give at most 2ⁿ stereoisomers.

scenes.heading: R/S vs E/Z

right.title: E / Z (alkenes)
points: Rank the two groups on each C

scenes.say: Both labels use the same priority rules: higher atomic number wins. For R and S, point the lowest group away and trace one, two, three, like a steering wheel. Clockwise is R. For alkenes, Z means zame zide: the top groups are together. E means opposite.
scenes.caption: Both labels use the same priority rules: higher atomic number wins. For R/S, point the lowest group away and trace 1 → 2 → 3, like a steering wheel. Clockwise is R. For alkenes, Z means 'Zame Zide': the top groups are together. E means opposite.

points: Skeletal: every corner and end is a carbon
Principal group gets the lowest locant
R/S and E/Z use CIP priorities
scenes.say: Quick recap. In skeletal structures, every corner is a carbon. The highest-priority group takes the suffix and the lowest locant. Four different groups make a stereocentre. And R, S, E and Z all use the same priority rules. Now try the practice questions!
